Chlorine gas is a strong oxidizing agent and sodium metal is an alkali metal. When they react, the chlorine gas oxidizes the sodium metal. The reaction is a redox reaction where chlorine gains electrons and sodium loses electrons. This reaction forms sodium hypochlorite (or sodium chlorate/sodium chlorate, depending on the exact conditions and stoichiometry, but the primary product in this simple reaction is sodium hypochlorite).
